```{r setup}
library(lab6knapsack)
```

## Runtime measurements
We measured elapsed time using `system.time()`. Data were generated before timing, using seed 42. Each result below is from a single run.

| Algorithm | Number of items | Capacity W | Elapsed time |
|:----------|----------------:|-----------:|-------------:|
| Brute force, original | 16 | 2000 | 0.30 s |
| Brute force, improved | 16 | 2000 | 0.15 s |
| Greedy | 1,000,000 | 3500 | 0.11 s |

Brute force examines every possible selection and returns an exact solution. Greedy ranks items by value per unit of weight and provides a fast approximation.

## Profiling and improvement
We profiled the brute-force function using `profvis`:
```{r profiling, eval=FALSE}
profvis::profvis({
  brute_force_knapsack(items16, W = 2000)
})
```

The profile highlighted time spent calculating total weights inside the loop. We extracted the weight and value columns once before the loop and reused those vectors, avoiding repeated column retrieval.

Elapsed time decreased from 0.30 to 0.15 seconds: an observed speedup of 2 and a 50% reduction in runtime. The algorithm still examines all possible selections. Repeated measurements would be needed to estimate the improvement more reliably.
